method: Linked official descriptions, CBS study p.57 and visually inspected museum plan/aerial/courtyard photographs. No third-party pixels distributed.

observations.observation: Sandstone carving and copper towers; original monumental courtyard fountain no longer exists.
Page 57 describes Trumpeter Tower as 59 m above courtyard, 62 m above water. Nine towers include four stair towers without spires and flat-topped Cannon/Telegraph Tower.
Museum plan distinguishes north forecourt, south-central Trumpeter, south-west Telegraph, north-west Kings Tower, south-east Pigeon Tower and chapel.
South-west aerial: broad flat Cannon Tower, steep copper wing roofs, ornate gables and high chimneys. Temporary scaffolding excluded.
Four separate roofed wings, open courtyard, taller central Trumpeter and green corner spires; red masonry bastion walls with grass crests.
Trumpeter octagonal shaft, balcony, bulb and two open lantern tiers. South courtyard chapel portal and pointed windows; shuttered roof gables.
Northern court gate, three window rows, pedimented frames, domed stair turret and two large ornate dormers.
